Diarium — The Uraniborg Diary, 1582–1597

A scholarly edition of the diary kept at Uraniborg from October 1582 to April 1597: the historical notes its scribes entered in the margin, each with the diary’s own words, its page in the printed edition and a link to the scan, graded A–C for the certainty of date and person; and the daily weather record the same book was kept for, day by day, verbatim.

248 historical notes, 1585–1597 · 136 persons indexed · 4,515 weather entries covering 4,849 days · 45 nights of the aurora · from the Vienna manuscript, Cod. 10718, through the edition of 1876

1Introduction

The book behind this chapter is a quarto of 191 leaves in the Austrian National Library, Vienna, Cod. 10718, bought for the Emperor Rudolf II in all probability on 28 October 1601, four days after Tycho’s death, and in the Hofbibliothek by 1652 at the latest. It is not in Tycho’s hand. His assistants kept it — for long stretches Elias Olsen Morsing, and after him a succession of others whose changes of hand the first editor marked (§9) — recording the state of the sky over Hven nearly every day from 1 October 1582 until the entries stop in mid-page on 22 April 1597, days after the household had moved to Copenhagen. A few of its leaves are Hven paper: the watermark shows Uraniborg over the word VRANIBVRGVM.

From 27 April 1585 the scribes also began to enter, in the margin and heavily abbreviated, the events of the island: arrivals and departures, a death, a wedding, the passing of the royal fleet. These historical notes are the visitor register of Uraniborg and the first half of this chapter. The weather entries they sit beside are the second half. Both were printed once, in 1876, from the Vienna manuscript, and again in 1927 in the ninth volume of the Opera Omnia; this chapter is built from the 1876 print and concorded to both.

How this chapter was made

Every historical note was extracted from the 1876 edition’s text and is printed here in the diary’s own words, with an English reading, the persons expanded where the editors or the diary itself expand them, and the printed page. The pages were verified by walking the whole diary day by day through the edition’s page breaks and locating each note’s text on its page; all but four of the notes were found on their page, and those four are placed by their day. Two entries that turned out to duplicate others under a wrong year or month were retired, one date was corrected against the print, and three notes that had been expanded were restored to what is printed. The weather record was parsed from the same text into one row per dated entry, keeping the early-modern Danish verbatim and adding only a small set of keyword flags, which are declared for what they are in §8.

The figures, and what they mean

FigureCountDefinition
Historical notes248one per marginal entry of an arrival, departure, death, event or movement, 1585–1597; an entry is a note, not a person and not a visit
Persons indexed136named persons in §4, folded across their name forms; a further 44 entries are unnamed persons and groups
… in the Familia pillar21persons whose record here links to the household prosopography
… with a VIAF record9persons with an authority id
Notes stating an origin or destination88§5
Printed pages carrying a note123of the 263 pages of the diary text in the 1876 edition
Editors’ footnotes53footnotes of the 1876 edition under the diary text (§9), plus 5 corrigenda
Entries in Rørdam’s register318persons and places in the 1876 index, concorded in §6
Weather entries4,515dated entries of the weather record; they cover 4,849 of the 5,318 days from 1 October 1582 to 22 April 1597, 469 days having no entry (§8)
Nights of the aurora45entries recording the chasmata (§8)

What these numbers are not. The register is not a count of visitors: one visit can produce two notes (an arrival and a departure) or none, and the scribes noted what interested them — Thoren observes that members of James VI’s entourage went out to Hven in the weeks after the King’s visit without any trace in the diary. It is not complete against its own source either: Tycho’s own comings and goings, which the diary records constantly, were excluded by rule when the register was compiled, and Rørdam’s index names persons on some forty printed pages where this register has nothing; both are set out in §10. A person with many entries is a person the scribes named often, not necessarily the most frequent guest. And the weather flags are keyword matches on a sixteenth-century vocabulary, useful for finding a day, never a climatology.

The grades

GradeNameAs applied in this chapterNotes
ASecurethe date and the person are both certain: the note names the person, or the editors identify them, and the day is not in doubt200
BProbableone element is uncertain — an initial or an abbreviation the editors could not expand, or a reading the print marks with a query46
CPossibleboth are uncertain, or the note is so abbreviated that the reading itself is in doubt2

Conventions

Dates. Every date is the diary’s, Julian (Old Style) throughout; the scribes never adopted the Gregorian reform. A note is dated to the day under whose weather entry it stands in the print.

Pages. “p. 143” is the printed page of the 1876 edition; the link opens that page of the Royal Danish Academy’s scan, whose PDF pages run 10 ahead of the print. The Opera Omnia page is given at month precision (§6).

Record keys. Every note prints its key (d-1590-03-20-a: the date, then a letter in the order of the notes under that day) and is addressable as #d-1590-03-20-a or ?entry=d-1590-03-20-a, which highlights it. Weather entries are keyed w-1590-03-20 and addressable as ?day=1590-03-20.

Excluded by rule. Tycho’s own departures and returns (abiit Hafniam, rediit) were not extracted unless a named companion is the event; the register therefore does not stand in for an itinerary, which is the Loca pillar’s business. The weather-only years before 27 April 1585 carry no historical notes.

2Catalogue of the historical notes

Every historical note in one table: the date, the diary’s words, the persons as expanded, the kind of event, the standing of the person, the place they came from or went to where the note says so, the printed page and the grade. Sort any column; filter by kind, standing, grade or year, or search the text; the count line states how many rows the filter leaves. The date opens the full record in §3.

3Register of the historical notes

The same notes in full, year by year. Each record prints its key, the diary’s own words, the reading, the persons with their links into the Familia pillar and to VIAF where an authority record exists, the origin or destination, the page in the 1876 edition with a link to that page of the Royal Danish Academy’s scan, the pages of the Opera Omnia reprint at month precision, and — where the edition’s footnote on that page names the person — the editors’ own identification in their words.

4Index of persons

One entry per person, across every form in which the scribes wrote the name — Soph. B., Domina S. B., Sophia Braa, Tychonis soror are one sister. The folding follows an alias table that is part of the published dataset; a form that matches no entry in it stands alone under its own name. Unnamed persons and groups (“two Scottish students”, “a nobleman sent by Heinrich Rantzau”) are gathered at the end. Each entry lists its notes by date, opening the record in §3, and links to the Familia pillar where the person is in the household prosopography.

5Origins and destinations

Where the diary says where a visitor came from or a departing guest was bound, the register records it. The places are given as the notes give them — a town, a province, a country — and are not located on a map, because the diary carries no coordinates and most of these names are regions. Notes without a stated origin or destination, the majority, are not counted here.

6Concordances

Three ways into the printed editions. First, H. F. Rørdam’s register of the historical notes, printed at the back of the 1876 volume, entry by entry with his page references — the prior index of these persons and places, and the standard by which the coverage of this register is measured. Second, the month-by-month concordance to the diary’s second printing in the Opera Omnia, whose pages are what most of the literature cites. Third, the map from the printed page to the page of the Academy’s scan, so that any page number in this chapter can be opened in the source.

8The weather series

The diary was kept for the weather; the historical notes are its margin. This section publishes the weather record in full: a figure of the sixteen years, the coverage of each year, the flags and how they were derived, the diary’s own vocabulary, the nights on which the scribes recorded the chasmata — the northern lights — the passages in which the diary itself accounts for a gap, and then every dated entry, verbatim, with its printed page.

The flags are keyword matches on the verbatim text and nothing more: an entry mentioning both morning cloud and afternoon sun carries both overcast and clear. The grid above colours each entry by one condition only, in the order snow, rain, frost, clear, overcast; the table is the record.

The vocabulary

Reading the early-modern Danish. mørckt / morckt overcast, dark · klart clear · graae / graaendis blowing — a graded wind term (sact / temmelig / hartt / megitt graaendis), parallel to blesendis and stormendis, classed by la Cour as wind force · regn rain · snee snow · frysendis / frost freezing · blest / storm wind, gale · thøe thaw · taage fog · chasmata / casmata / kasmata the aurora · winds: synden S, norden N, østen E, vesten W, norduest NW, sudost SE · den ganttske dag the whole day · om afftenen in the evening · om natten at night. The Opera Omnia volume carries a full Index vocum Danicarum (pp. 329–343).

21 Feb 1584p. 33Rett skye ferst om morgenn omkring 0 , med temmelig vestenn graae; om nattenn vor dit aldelis stille whær och smuck klart till epther mindnat, sidenn opkomme der chasmata och skyernne och begynte nogit at blesze, frost.
2 Mar 1584p. 34Morcktt fuctig, om natten epther midnat opkomme der mange kasmata, som regierit mogit den ganske nat; suduest.
23 Mar 1584p. 35Mørckt denn ganske dag, temmelig graaindis whær; om affthennenn vor dit klaartt till mindnat; sidenn opkomme der chasmata et skyernne.
12 Apr 1584p. 36Dunckell till middag, om midaffthen bleff dit herlig klartt, och vaarit ochsaa om nattenn till epther mindnat, siden op­ komme der chasmata och skyernne aff nordenn och vor dit stille.
16 Apr 1584p. 36Herlig klartt denn ganske dag nestenn østenn; om nattenn mørckt till mindnat, sidenn bleff dit smuct klartt; dog op­ komme der vndertidenn mange chasmata.
22 Apr 1584p. 37Klartt; om nattenn epthermindnat opkomme chasmata, som forsammeltis supra verticem circa lucidam Lyræ; nogit graait det aff syndenn.
31 Jan 1585p. 48Regenn først om dagenn, siden begynte hort at blesse, som vaarit framdelis denn ganske nat, och vor dit om natten till mindnat klartt; men der opkomme mange kasmata aff nordenn, och omkring ( ginge der halones; graaindis suduest.
12 Dec 1585p. 61Smaa Regenn och fuctig whæderlig till mod 11 slet, sidenn mort med temmelig graaindis suduest; mod affthennenn regnit dit atter sacteligenn igienn. Om affthennenn vid 7 slet skildis skyernne nogit att, och der komme mange Chasmata aff norden och for offuer den ganske himmel, postquam ad verticem ascen- dissent ab Aquilone; in Austrum vsque ad æquatorem & paulo infra descenderunt postea per totum sparsa coelum mirifice concurrebant et sursum se attollerunt præsertim circa H. 8 ab omni plaga mundi. — H. 9 eum iam coelum nubibus magis esset immune et serenius ad lucidam caudæ Cygni congredi videbantur. Non diu tarnen in vno certo aliquo loco commorabantur. In Aquilone interdum tanquam gladii conspiciebantur primum parua, postea in magnam molem exereuerunt et quasi ad inuicem dimicabant. Fuerunt fere Chasmata semper eiusdem coloris ad albedinem nonnihil ver- gentis. — H. tranquilla et minus concurrere videbantur. Quæ ad Aquilonem apparebant magis fuerunt lucida. — H. 94 apud lucidam Capellæ non procul a vértice distantem aliquamdiu consistere videbantur. — H. 10| disparere prorsus videbantur et illorum vestigium apud Aquilonem solummodo remansit, tune erat bene serenum. — H. 10| coelum densis nubibus obductum est. — H. 2 rursus fuit aliqua serenitas, et chasmata rursus exorta tanquam Lunæ splendor ædes illumi- narunt. Postea evenerunt, non tarnen fuerunt adeo copiosa vt ad vesperas. Thenne ganske nat graait dit hort aff west suduest. Mod dag temmelig klart, sidenn mort igienn.
3 Feb 1586p. 66Klartt thenn ganske dag, stille; om nattenn opkomme der først nordenn kasmata, sidenn aff søndenn och drøff sactelig offuer then ganske himmel sine concursu magno, sed in gyrum circa H. 12 conuolui videbantur; mod dagh bleff dit aldelis mort och begyntt att graae aff sudost. ?
4 Feb 1586p. 66Mørckt thenn ganske dagh mogit hort stormindis sudost; mod affthenn bleff dit stor snee fagh, som vaarit mesten part thenn ganske nat. Signa huius tempestatis triduum antea in occasu et postea in chasmatis apparuerunt.
29 Jun 1586p. 73Milt, temmelig klart, sact suduest, Epthermiddag regenn; circa occasum Q apparuit iris; om nattenn vor der mange kasmata per totum coelum concurrentia. Abiit Regina.
2 Sep 1586p. 76Mørckt och klartt tillsammenn, nordenn, om nattenn opkomme der mange kasmata.

21 Aug 1590p. 157Nordvest, themelige stor graade och solskien vndertiiden. Noctu circiter hor. 9. et 10mam casmata ardebant quæ ob ortu incipientia, medium usque coelum conscenderunt; deinde per totum fere coelum sparsa nubes undiquaque rariusculas in suis limitibus constrinxerunt.
30 Aug 1590p. 158Nordwest, smuckt stille och nogett Solskienn, om afften klardt et coelum unterdum undique Casmatis transcurrentibus in nostro hemisphærio occnpatum, quæ postea in nubes conversa rariusculas videbantur. Vesperi nobiscum observabat D. Tycho, item Rothmannus.
1 Sep 1590p. 158Nordvest smuckt stille och klardt, mod afften nordost, om natten klardt och store casmata y norden. Abiit Rothmannus.
2 Sep 1590p. 158Sudwest, nogit graade och lidett Solskien om dagen undertiden mod afften Sudost, forst om natten nogit klardt blessinde och Casmata.
21 Sep 1590p. 160Nordvest, thiunde skyer och nogit solskien egienem, item nogit lidett graade; om efftermeddag smuckt klart, item mest parten aff natten, klart. Observabamus crepusculum vesper- tinum. Casmata visa sunt in septent. Abiit Villihelmus N.
22 Sep 1590p. 160Nordnorost, smuck lunitt och klart aldelis om morgen, siden sudost och klaidt den helle Dag. Item om natten klart, et Casmata in sept. visa. Accessit Christophorus chirurgus Haf.
9 Nov 1590p. 164Sudost, lidett blessende och imod meddag nogitt Solskien, siden vklartt, først om afften nogit stiernliust, siden aldelis vklart. Casmata in septentrione videbantur. Giorgius Brochenhus abiit Roschildiam.
14 Nov 1590p. 164Vesten klartt och lidett blessende den helle dag egiennem, om afftenen forst nogit lidett klartt, siden Casmata fere offuer allt och møgit graade med regn mod dag.
10 Dec 1590p. 166Vestenvind, stille och themelige klart solskienn om dagenn, om afftenen forst lidett klartt, siden om natten vklardt och tageactiige. Hac vespera íj achronychium observaturi, vidimus in oriente 20 circiter grad, supra nostrum horizontem casmata vel potius phasmata insolitæ apparentiæ rubra scilicet, instar coccinei coloris, quæ 4 horæ durabant. apparebant enim paulo ante 7mam ortum circa inferiores pedes II ducentia atque ita per tjnum (ubi maxima visa sunt) Aldeboranque obliqui ascendendo, sub Pleiadibus tandem evanuerunt h. 8|. Visa sunt eodem tempore et alia sólita casmata hæc suo discursu attingentia interdum ac occultantia.
17 Dec 1590p. 167Nordost, nogitt graade och solskienn vndertidenn om nattenn klart och casmata och hart frost. Accessit Dominus Jacobus Coronensis.
16 Feb 1591p. 170Nordost, snee om morgenn tillig themelige hartt graade och frøst, siden mest solskien om dagen; om natten klartt. Apparebat in altitudine circiter 10° et quantitate satis magna. NB. Hac vespera post (æ occasum Chasmata in septemtrione circa horizontem prodibant, inter quæ ad ortum magis vergentia rubra erant. Circiter mediam vero noctem altius ascendebant & totum' hemisphærium nostrum atque horizontem ubique mira saltatione ac concursu perstringebant. — Vide ad 10 diem Decemb. superioris anni, ubi similia apparebant Casmata.
19 Feb 1591p. 171Østenn, klartt den helle Dag et eadem omnino facies coeli aërisque qvæ fuit heri et nudius tertius. Casmata vesperi rubra.
22 Feb 1591p. 171Nordost, klartt, hartt frost och graendis, om natten ochsaa klart och Casmata.
2 Apr 1591p. 174Vestnordvest hartt graade, solskien mesten part och frost, om afftenn forst klartt. Hac vespera horam circiter nonam Casmata vidimus e meri- dionali Coeli plaga paululum supra horizontem exaltata, idque contra naturam loci iis ut plurimum in septemtrione deputati, oriri. Coloris sane inusitati & fere omnigeni, primum enim conspiciebantur ut soient flamea subalbescentia, postea rubra vel sanguinea, denique violi colorem induebant, coelique verti- cem culminabant dehinc partim ad septentrionem descendentia hemisphærium undique nostrum occupabant. NB. Vide ad diem 16 Martii et 10 Decembris anni superioris. Abiit famulus Soph. B. cum Erico Landt

The diary’s own account of its gaps 8 passages

Where the daily record lapses, the scribe sometimes summarises the missing weeks in a sentence; these are the passages, at the entry that carries them.

1–3 Sep 1585 (p. 56) — entry
Hisce diebus nobis apparuit plærumque nubilum coelum cum pluuioso aëre atque occidentali increpante vento.
6 Jun 1589 (p. 125) — entry
Graendis nordwest och wklarhed med kuld, efftermiddag stormendis westen. Sois Regnbogen H. 4, et Qle jam in horizonte existente occidentali iris in meridie apparuit, sed pars saltem. eaque obscure admodum. T. red. NB. Hisce diebus ab ultimo Maji scilicet hucusque fre- qventius videbatur iris vel dupla et qvidem interdum ter in die etc.
7 Sep 1593 (p. 214) — entry
Sudost, wklart till mod dag om natten. NB. Per has duas fere septimanas, qvibus dierum numeratio intermissa est, fuit fere única aëris constitutio, videlicet nebu­ losa ac pluviosa, flantibus vehementer Zephyro ac Coro, adeo ut Cymbæ per aliquot dies retentas sint Helsingoram Haf- niamque transfretandæ.
7 Oct 1593 (p. 215) — entry
Blessendis aff sudost; mod afften oc om natten Stoer Storm oc Regen. Hisce diebus intermediis, qvibus singulis status coeli et aëris non assignatur, fuit fere eadem coeli facies, videlicet obscura et nimbricosa (?)’ fiante ut plurimum subsolano — idque interdum validius interdum vero remissius. 0 au tern parum aut fere nullo die clare splendidit ñeque noctu ulla serenitas præter- quam die 12 Octobris et multæ pluviæ postea.
8 Nov 1593 (p. 215) — entry
Sudost oc morck veder, blessendes nogett mod affthen. Dette efftherfolgendis tid vdi dette Aar baffuer mest veritt 1593 — 1594. forvden vden nogen winther; thi dett haffuer inthett frosset; vinden mett Stor storm regen oc Vwer haffuer det hart idelig verett oc vinden mest aff sonden oc vesten.
1–5 Nov 1595 (p. 240) — entry
Hisce intermidiis diebus, qvibus aëris mutationes non assignantur, non erat notabilis aliqua mutatio, sed coeli fere eadem facies et aëris.
30 Aug 1596 (p. 255) — entry
Smucktt stille oc klartt ver. Hisce intermediis diebus Hafniæ fuimus et fuit aëris constitutio tranqvilla et coeli facies varia.
21 Mar 1597 (p. 263) — entry
Norden noget blesendis. Registeret vi alle junkers bøger. Hisce intermissis diebus fuit varia aëris constitutio, quam propter alias occupationes observasse aut notasse non potuimus.

12 DecSWaurora, rain, clear, overcastSmaa Regenn och fuctig whæderlig till mod 11 slet, sidenn mort med temmelig graaindis suduest; mod affthennenn regnit dit atter sacteligenn igienn. Om affthennenn vid 7 slet skildis skyernne nogit att, och der komme mange Chasmata aff norden och for offuer den ganske himmel, postquam ad verticem ascen- dissent ab Aquilone; in Austrum vsque ad æquatorem & paulo infra descenderunt postea per totum sparsa coelum mirifice concurrebant et sursum se attollerunt præsertim circa H. 8 ab omni plaga mundi. — H. 9 eum iam coelum nubibus magis esset immune et serenius ad lucidam caudæ Cygni congredi videbantur. Non diu tarnen in vno certo aliquo loco commorabantur. In Aquilone interdum tanquam gladii conspiciebantur primum parua, postea in magnam molem exereuerunt et quasi ad inuicem dimicabant. Fuerunt fere Chasmata semper eiusdem coloris ad albedinem nonnihil ver- gentis. — H. tranquilla et minus concurrere videbantur. Quæ ad Aquilonem apparebant magis fuerunt lucida. — H. 94 apud lucidam Capellæ non procul a vértice distantem aliquamdiu consistere videbantur. — H. 10| disparere prorsus videbantur et illorum vestigium apud Aquilonem solummodo remansit, tune erat bene serenum. — H. 10| coelum densis nubibus obductum est. — H. 2 rursus fuit aliqua serenitas, et chasmata rursus exorta tanquam Lunæ splendor ædes illumi- narunt. Postea evenerunt, non tarnen fuerunt adeo copiosa vt ad vesperas. Thenne ganske nat graait dit hort aff west suduest. Mod dag temmelig klart, sidenn mort igienn.p. 61
13 DecSWrain, clear, overcastMort fuctigh, temmelig suduest graae; mod middag skildis skyernne nogit att, och 0 skiennde lidit, siden mort igienn till mod affthenn, daa ginge 0 rødt neder. Om affthen klartt och nyenn apparuit pallida et nonnihil rubicunda; vin­ denn sactedis nogit och blæste icki saa hort som om dagen; vid 10 slet bleff dit mørt igienn, mod dagenn begynte dit at regne och graait nogit horder ind som tillforn om nattenn aff suduest.p. 62

Magnitudo eius nonnihil minor sole erat. — Color erat purpu- reus et rubicundus tarn parelii quam portionis solis apparentis, splendebat propemodum vt ipse Sol nec facile eum aliquis intueri potuit. — Altitudo eius supra horizontem erat quasi trium graduum. Ascendebant ab ipso sole ad idolum radii qui erant densi et eiusdem coloris cum 0 e et parelio. — Prout 0 paulatim occidebat ita diminuebatur, cum de sole nihil videri et quasi eclipsari videbatur, donee totus euanuit, interiecto nostro horizonte visuali inter solem et parelium. 6 MaySWrainSudvest vind med støbregn fra klocken vor fire om morgen indtill 8, der nest stille till effter medag, saa kom ther igien en synden vin med stor regn, huilcken warde vid 1^ thime siden temelig grade alf sønden. Sophia Brahe abiit mane hor. 7.p. 147
7 MayNWrain, overcastNordvest wind, mørckt med regn moxen den helle dag och tycke skyer, mod afften vendis vinden till sudvest.p. 147
8 Mayclear, overcastSudwest wind med nogle tycke skyer; mod meddag klart, dog nogle skyer huos horizonten. Mod afften smock stille weder och klardt. Abiit Casparus in Schaniam primo dilucido.p. 147
9 MaySErain, clear, overcastSudsudost stille vindt och temelig klart end till efftermeddag, dog saa att der var eblant nogle skyer hos horizonten, siden mod afften mørckt och hemelen offuerdragen med skyer. Vinden aff sudost och begynte hart att graade och den till- komendes naat saa lige vd till en stor regn. Lunam circa horizontem in alitudine quasi 1^ nubes in modum Zonæ duobus in locis obducebant. Famuli J. et N. propter neqvitiam se alius alium mutuo virgis nudi exipiebant.p. 147
10 MaySErain, overcastOm morgen vid siu slett begynte dett att regne aff sudost och holt siden med et stuor regn till horam 11, siden om efftermeddag solsken och sagt vind, dog var der nogle skyer. Casparus rediit. Johannes famulus dimiltitur venia Thyconis.p. 147
11 MaySEovercastSudost themelige klardt, mod afften grade med thycke skyer och lidet regen vid 10 slett P. M.p. 147
12 MaySErain, overcastSudost nogit graade mørck och noget regen for Meddag. siden sactis vinden nogit, mørckt, och saa vd till regn; det regnet och nogit mod afften.p. 148
13 MayErain, overcastØstenn vinndt forst om Morgenn themelige graade med thonnde skyer under gandske hemelen, siden om effter Medag hårdt graade och tycke skyer lig till regn.p. 148
14 MaySWrain, overcastSudvest vind themelige Stille, om morgen thynde skyer under hemelen, mod affthenn begynte at graade och regne nogett y Eletall. H. 7 P. M. duplex iris conspecta est. Puer Aurifabri diem obiit h. 3 a. M.p. 148
15 MaySEclearSudsudost vind themelig klart formeddag, sidenn icki saa klart thi hemelen nubibus raris subductum fuit.p. 148
16 MaySEovercastSudost, themelige graade wklardt den helle dag.p. 148
17 MayNWclear, overcastForst om morgen nordvest, deslige klardt stille vindt, der nest mod meddag sudost, lidett graade och nogit vklart.p. 148
18 MayWovercastVestenn Vklardt och temelige graade, om natten themelig stille och nogit klardt. Johannes Aurifaber cum uxore Hafniam abiit.p. 148
19 MayNWovercastVestnordvest themelige graade och thycke skyer vnder alt hemelen in nostro hemisphærio, om naten stille.p. 148
20 MaySEclear, overcastSudsudost vind, lidet graade och themelig klart, dog hos horizontem skyerne. Hafnia nos inviserunt D. Nicolaus Krag. M. Jonasp. 148
21 MayNWclear, overcastSudost vind, først nogit klart, sidenn om efftermidag nord­ nordvest themelige stille och nogle store skyer.p. 148
22 MaySWclear, overcastSudvest lidett graade och vklart med stuore skyer, vndertiden Solskenn. Abierunt hospites Hafnienses remanente tarnen M. Michaele chi- rurgo. — Vesperi Scoti nobiles accesserunt.p. 148
23 MaySrain, overcastSønden vind themelige grade och begynde dett att regne der ) Formodentlig Jonas Venusinus. klocken var vid 10, sidenn støre graade och regnit dett lidett wid siu siett om afften. Abiit M. Michael Hafniam. Discesserunt nobiles scoti Helsing- oram et cum illis Arnoldus F.p. 148
24 MayNWclear, overcastSudost vinnd, nogit graade, sidenn mod meddag nordvest ; item om efftermeddag en stund ost nordost, siden vesten och Stille, undertiden nogit solskien, ellers aldelis uklart.p. 149
25 MaySEovercastSudost vind, lidet graade och nogit solskind, om naten themelige klardt. Sophia Brahe hue accessit.p. 149
26 MayNWclear, overcastNordvest vind themelige graade och smuekt klardt solskeen, dog saa att der vare nogle skyer hos horizonten; om nathen smukt stille och klart.p. 149
27 MaySEovercastSudost vind, graade och vklardt den gandske dag.p. 149
28 MayNWrain, clear, overcastFørst osten vind, lidett regn och vklardt, siden om effther- medag sudvest och vklart, nogit graade altid; item nordvest, vest lidet regn och graade mod afften.p. 149
29 MayNWovercastVestnordvest, themelige graade och nogit solskien. Discessit Socpia B. in Sconiam et cum ea Mar. Ingildi Coroniam.p. 149
30 MayNWrain, clearNordvest hart graendis och klart solskien undertiden, om natten mod dag regn.p. 149
31 MayNWclearSmukt stille vind, først vesten, siden mod Meddag sønden och klart soelskien; siden vendis vinden till nordvest, saa om igien till sudost enden en halff time, existente serenitate pri­ stina et tranqvillitate. Johannes Bilde, consobrinus Tychonis et Mathias scriba Coronia hue accesserunt circa horam 5 et cum iis Mar. rediit.p. 149
1 Junclear, overcastSüdsüdost, themelige graade och klart den helle dag, mod afftenn smukt stille och klart om natten.p. 149
2 JunSEclear, overcastSudost, smuk klart och Stille moxen, om efftermeddag lidett graade. Discessit Joh. Bilde et Malh. scriba.p. 149
3 JunSWrain, clear, overcastVestsudvest, themelige graade och vklart først om morgen, mod Meddag kom en stuor regn med blest ind till 3 siett, siden nogit klart och blest. Accessit circa merid. M. Martinus Pleciusp. 150
4 JunWclear, overcastVestnordtvest vinnd, haart graade och vklart. om efftermeddag klart solskien och nogit mindre grade. Regias naves qvasdam e Scotia reversas Hafniamque versus navi­ gantes vidimus.p. 150
5 JunNWovercastNordnordvest, klardt och nogit graade till mod affthen, syden smock stille och nogle skyer hos horizontem. Discesserunt hospites Haterslevienses.p. 150
6 JunSWclear, overcastSudvest vind themelige graade och alldelis vklardt, om effter­ meddag nogit klart och Solskienn.p. 150
7 JunNWovercastNordvest Solskienn och nogit lidit graade, mod affthen thycke Skyer aff nordvest et parelion a parte solis septentrionali visum est.p. 150
8 JunWrain, clearVesten vind themelige stille och lidett regn om morgen vid 8 siett aldelis vklart, siden om effthermiddag nogit klart solskien, om natten nogit regn.p. 150
9 JunNEclear, overcastNordost uklart, mod meddag lidett graade, mod afften nord­ vest en halff stund, siden ostsudost, morckt, skye och nogit thorden, om natten synden.p. 150
10 JunNWovercastVestnordvest, themelige graade och nogit solskien den ganndske dag, dog mod afften nogit stillere, om natten liunet.p. 150
11 JunNWclearNordvest och lidet solskin, om afften och natten vklart.p. 150
12 JunNWclearNordvest, vklart och smuck stille om morgen och paa dagen siden solskien, siden mod afften erat obductum coelum rarius- culis nubibus ad utrumque polum fere meridianorum instar dispositis. Jacobus Holst Haffniensis mercator hue accessit.p. 150
13 JunNWclear, overcastVestnordvest, themelige stille och smuck veder, vklart ined nogle thynde skyer huilcke Solen dog skiende nogit igienem. M. Nicolaus rediit Hafniæ, relicto Aurifabro Jo.p. 151
14 JunWclear, overcastSmuk stille och klart om morgen, siden effter meddag thernelig hart graade aff vesten; om afften klart och stille.p. 151
15 JunSWclearSudvest smukt klart och stille den helle dag om natten och klart och stille. Hafnia hue accesserunl M. Christoph. Chymist^ M. Johan architectus.p. 151
16 JunWclearVesten vind, mest klart och themelige stille den gandske dag. Abiit Tycho in Scaniam, abierunlque simul Hafnienses hospites.p. 151
17 JunNWclear, overcastNordvest, themelige graade och klart, dog nogit dunkelt och taageactigt den helle dag.p. 151
18 JunNWclear, overcastNordvest, themelige stille och klart dog den helle dag och mogit dunkelt och taageactig, sole hac vespera 4 vel 5 grad, ab hori­ zonte usque dum occiderat sangvineum colorem repræsentante.p. 151
19 JunNNordnorvest consimilis tam coeli qvam auræ facies cum die præcedente.p. 151
20 JunNWclear, overcastNordvest, stille, klart och dunkelt, siden sønden och begynte lidett att graade.p. 151
21 JunNWrain, clear, overcastNordvest dunckelt om morgen och themelige stille, emod middage nogett graade och en støb regn, som vor hen ved ett Stund, siden nogit klart och graade den natt. Rediit Tycho Coroniam.p. 151
22 JunNWovercastVestnordvest, klardt och themelige Stuor graade, mod afften nogit sacter graade. Rediit Tycho sero vesperis.p. 151
23 JunNWclear, overcastVestnordvest themelige graade thill meddag, siden smucht sagt vindt och klart den helle dagh.p. 151
24 JunSovercastSønden vindt themelige klardt och lidett graade, om morgenn thaage offuer haffuit, som siden slogis op y veyrit, siden om dagen nogen smaa pletter aff skyerne paa himelen.p. 151
25 JunNovercastSüdsüdost vind, klardt och nogit graade thill mod afften, siden stille och nogle thynde skyer hos Horizontem, besyn­ derlige om ( vdi vester och nord.p. 151
26 JunNWclear, overcastSudsudost vind, themelige graade och dunckelactige klart, mod aff. sact stille och klart; vendis vinden om till nordvest.p. 152
27 JunNEclearNordnordost, nogett thaage om morgen, siden klart och mogit hædt den gandske dag, om nathen klardt. Uxor Pauli pharmacopolæ domum abil vesperi.p. 152
28 JunNWovercastNordvest stille och klardt, mod aff. nogle skyer y vesten om Q hos horizontem. Abiil Tycho Hafniam.p. 152
29 JunNWovercastNordvest, themelige graade och klardt, dog saa att der var thynde skier allevegne moxen under himelen in nostro hemisphærio.p. 152
30 JunNclear, overcastNorden, om morgen nogle skyer och themelige stille veder, siden themelige klart och moxen aldelis stille den helle dag och mogit hedt. Accesserunl duo Germani studiosi circa Hor 3. — Rediit Tycho Hafnia vesperi.p. 152
1 JulovercastSudwest vindt, nogit graade och themelige klardt, dog hos horizontem allevegne dunkelactige vklardt.p. 152
2 JulSWclear, overcastSudost vind, om morgen mogit taage, siden paa dagen solskien och dunckel actige, mod afften sudvest och vklart allevegne hos horizontem, stille. Item smockt stille. Hab. con. Jo.p. 152
3 JulSWrain, overcastSønden vindt om morgen stille och taage, siden themelige graade och Solskien, om affthen sudvest och ett smukt regn.p. 152
4 JulWrain, overcastVesten, themelige stuor graade och regn emellum vndertiden denn helle dag, mod afften themelig stille och regnn.p. 152
5 JulSWrain, clear, overcastSudvest om morgen och en møgett stuor regn vid ij siett. Siden mod meddag vendis vinden till sudost och regnede och smuckt, ad meddag lidett graade med regn, siden mere regn om eftermeddag, om naten uklart och nogit graade.p. 152
6 JulNWovercastVestnordvest, underthiden Solskiend och themilige graade den helle Dagh.p. 152
7 JulSWovercastSudvest, om morgen themelige stille och nogit solskien, siden paa dagen vklardt och graade. Deliqvium Lunæ, eodem die mane futurum nullum plane animadvertentes deprehendimus supra nostrum horiz. Venil tabellar. Prag.p. 153
8 JulSWSudvest, om morgen och afften smuckt stille och vklardt om dagen, och vklardt och lidett grade, om naten klardt.p. 153
9 JulOm Morgen nogit klardt, sidenn vklardt till 10 siett, dereffter klardt igien den ganndske dag sudwest vind och hedt, om naten klardt.p. 153
10 JulWovercastOm morgen vesten, Smuckt stille och klardt, siden themelige graade och stuore skyer vndertiden : om afften themeligh klardt, siden om natten vklardt. Rediit D. Petrus e Seelandia.p. 153
11 JulNWovercastOm morgen Nordt, themelige graade och uklardt, siden temelige klardt och sagt stille nordvest.p. 153
12 JulNWclear, overcastNordvest vind, om morgen vklart aldelis och nogit graade, siden nogett Solskien och om afftenen noget klart och stille aldelis naten offuer.p. 153
13 JulNWclear, overcastNordnordvest vind, stille och klart om morgen, siden den gandtske dag dunckelactig taage et minus desicata aura. Sophie B. et D. Nicolaus Crag. Hafnia advenerunl.p. 153
14 JulSWclearFørst om Morgen Sudost, stille och dunckelactig, klart, siden sudvest och klardt østen møgit heede den ganske dag. Abiil Soph. B. domum remanente D. N. Kragio.p. 153
15 JulSWovercastOm morgen sudost stille och dunckellactige klardt indtill effter meddag. Siden en Stuor thorden och lunit med nogit regen; vinden aff sudvest och nogit graade. Om natten thorden och lunit. Accessit consul Roschildensis cum alio qvodam suo concivi actum s de causa Erasmi. *)p. 153
16 JulSErain, clear, overcastOm morgen sudost vind och stuor støb regn till mod meddag; siden tbørveder och nogett solskien, mod afften lidett graade och vklart. Abiit D. Nicolaus Cragius et cum eo Tycho Tychonides tune primum Scholæ apud Surenses inaugurandus.p. 154
17 JulSErain, overcastSudost, themelige graade och klardt forst om morgen Stuore skyer och nogit regn effter meddag mod afften Sudwest vklardt och graade, om natten vklardt. Venit aulicus famulus ab Othone Brokenhus.p. 154
18 JulSWSudsudvest, om morgen nogit grade och Solskyen, siden vklardt, vinden sudsudost och nogit grade den helle dag. Abiit Servus Oth. Bro.p. 154
19 JulSWVesten sudvest, om morgen themeligt klardt siden vklardt och nogit grade den dag och natt. Venit Ilenricus Mum, civis Hafniensis.p. 154
20 JulWclearVesten vindt, vklart. dog nogit. Solskien och lidet grade, om aff. klardt tliemelig och stille. Venit sive potius rediit Casparus Suinderin mane.p. 154
21 JulSWclearSudvest vind, om morgen vklardt siden smuekt klardt och der effter dunckelactig; vinden till sudost, om natten themelig klart. Eclipsin 01!s observavimus circiter h. 8 A. M.p. 154
22 JulSErain, overcastSudost, om morgen themeligh klardt och lidet grade, mod afften vklardt och mere graade, om natten thorden regn. Abiit Valentinus opere aggeris apud. molendinum confecto. — Venit Avlicus cimber Petrus civis Arhusiensis.p. 154
23 JulSWclearSudvest, themelige klardt och heede mod afften liden kalder blest, om natten stille och klartt.p. 154
24 JulSErain, clearSudost Solskien først om dagenn, sidenn strax meddag regenn, mod afften nogit klart (gien, om natten Lunit, thorden och regn. M. Niels Kolding, om hvad der var passeret, da „min Tiener Rasmus Persen, som nu er udi Gonsøgaard, havde udsendt to Mænd af Roskilde til mig, Borgemester Christen Skyt og Peder Sverdfeger“, efterdi de [nemlig Krag og Kolding] vare da tilstede. — Gonsøgaard er ritneligviis nuværende Heinstrupgaard.p. 154
25 JulSEovercastSudost, regen och nogit graade den helle dag moxen, siden meddag var vinden aff Südsüdwest.p. 155
26 JulNWrain, overcastNordvest lidett graade och nogit solskien, mod aff. lidett regn och stercker vind den helle natt offner. Tycho Hafniam. Venit S. B. confestim post Tychonis dis- cessum.p. 155
27 JulNWclear, overcastNordvest themelige graade och nogit Solskien den helle dagh. om naten vklart. Venerunl tres studiosi Mgri. Argentinenses. — Abiit Sophia B. Hafniam.p. 155
28 JulSEovercastSudsudost, smuckt klardt och lidett graade mod afftenn vklardt och om nattenn. Abierunt peregrini studiosi Helsingoram.p. 155
29 JulSEovercastOm morgen sudost themelige stille och solskien, siden adskiellig wederskiffte den helle dag underthiden aff norwest, under- thiden aff synden; om afften graade och lunild. Rediil Sophia B. Hafnia.p. 155
30 JulovercastSudwest themelig Stuor graade och nogitt Solskienn den helle dag.p. 155
31 JulNovercastOm morgen vestenn, themelige graade och nogit Solskien. Siden norden och en stor graade den natt offuer, item vklardt.p. 155
1 AugNWovercastNordvest themelige graade och nogit Solskien den helle dag, om afftenen och natten Stille. Rediit Tycho vesperi cum Rothmanno *\ Landtgravii Mathematico.p. 155
2 AugSWSudvest stille Solskien och møgit hede om nathen themeligt klardt.p. 155
3 AugSudwest, smuckt klardt och stille Dagenn egiemen. Disligist och om natten. Accès ser unt quatuor studiosi Germani, M. Johannes Rungellius ') Christofer Rothmann, Hofastronom hos Landgrev Wilhelm IV i Hessen. Isnachsensis, Johannes Hippius Bergensis ad Viram, Bertholdus Rudingerus Hertzfeldianus, Matthias Biotins Polonus.p. 155
4 AugSEovercastSudost, smuck klardt først om morgen, siden och solskien med nogle skier undertiden och nogit lidett graade.p. 156
5 AugSEclearOstsudost och sudsudost, vndertidenn smuckt klart och stille denn helle dag.p. 156
6 AugSESudost, om morgen noget solskien siden vklardt stille och mod afften nogit regen och om natten wklardt.p. 156
7 AugSErain, storm, overcastSudost, themelige Stuor graade och stuor Regn undertiden moxen den helle Dage, mod natten klardt indtilll mod Dag igien. Siden regn och hastige storm.p. 156
8 AugSEovercastSudost vindt, nogett graade och wklardt.p. 156
9 AugNclear, overcastNordwest vinnd, liden graade och nogitt klart, dog icki aldelis. Accessit Guilihelmus Kett cum tribus aliis comitibus, inter qvos unus erat mercator Scotus. alter qui antea hic fuit, doctus nobilis vocatus Georgius Gedde. Hic discesserunt eadem vespera. Acces- serunt et alii quatuor Helsingora, inter qvos unus, Christophorus a Valrott Borusius, doctus adolescens et peregrinus nobilis fuit, cœleris etiam nobilibus, sed Coroneburgæ arcis satellitibus, duorum horum nomina hcec fuere Johannes Schrotten, Christophorus Siletius; hi apud nos pernoctarunt.p. 156
10 AugSEovercastSudost, smuckt hedt och klardt den helle dag, om natten vid midnatt vklardt och beginte nogit att graade.p. 156
11 AugSEclear, overcastOstsudost, themilige graade och wklart, mod afften themelige stille och om natenn klardt.p. 156
12 AugSEovercastSudost themelige graade och solskienn mod afften stille och først om natten klardt.p. 156
13 AugEOstenn, stille och solskien den helle dag, om naten klardt. Disces sit Tycho in Scaniam cum Ro ih. et Lavonio.p. 156
14 AugNEclearNordost, klardt, stille och hede den dag och om natten stille och klart. T. venil.p. 156
15 AugEOsten vind, klardt och stille, disligist och om natten.p. 156
16 AugSErain, clearNorden, om morgen thaage, siden sudsudost stille hedt och solskien, mod aff. vklardt och nogit liditt regnn, om natten vklart.p. 157
17 AugSEclear, overcastSudost, om morgen vklart, dog nogit solskien och nogit lidett graade, om natten vklart. Rediit Tycho e Scania.p. 157
18 AugSErain, overcastSudost, vklardt stille om morgen siden nogit graade och om efftermeddag nogit regn aff vesten.p. 157
19 AugSWrain, overcastSudvest vklardt och nogit graade om morgen, siden om effter­ meddag store graade och regn, item om natten regn. Abiit Hafniam 37. TV.p. 157
20 AugSWrain, storm, overcastSudvest, vklardt hart graade och regn vnderthiden den helle dagh, om natten hefftige storm.p. 157
21 AugNWaurora, overcastNordvest, themelige stor graade och solskien vndertiiden. Noctu circiter hor. 9. et 10mam casmata ardebant quæ ob ortu incipientia, medium usque coelum conscenderunt; deinde per totum fere coelum sparsa nubes undiquaque rariusculas in suis limitibus constrinxerunt.p. 157
22 AugWovercastVesten vindt, wklardt och nogett graade den helle dag.p. 157
23 AugSEovercastSudost, først om dagen themelige graade och nogit lidett solskien, siden vklardt osten, om afftenen nogit klardt; circa mediam noctem horrenda tonitrua audiebantur.p. 157
24 AugSWclear, overcastSudvest vklart och themelige graade, om natten nogit store graade och mod dag nogit klardt.p. 157
25 AugSWrain, overcastSudvest vindt themelige haart graade och nogit solskien iblandt store driffue Skyer och nogit regn. Hic accessit nobilis quidam Germanus, Caroli Ducis Austria legatus. cui nomen Hieronimus Mogaslerus.p. 157
26 AugSovercastSudwest vind, themelige blessinde och vklardt, dog emellum skyerne vndertiden Solskienn, om afften Syndenn. Discessit idem nobilis.p. 157
27 AugSWovercastSudvest vind, nogit graade och vklardt, om afftenn taageactige och nogit klardt. Venit nobilis germanis discessitque.p. 157
28 AugSWSudsudvest blæssindis och wklardt denn helle dagh, item om natten.p. 158
29 AugWrain, overcastVestsudwest, wklardt och nogett graade, mod afften ett lidett fog regnn. Iris quatriplex in oriente. De imperato focus incendebatur in culina.p. 158
30 AugNauroraNordwest, smuckt stille och nogett Solskienn, om afften klardt et coelum unterdum undique Casmatis transcurrentibus in nostro hemisphærio occnpatum, quæ postea in nubes conversa rariusculas videbantur. Vesperi nobiscum observabat D. Tycho, item Rothmannus.p. 158
31 AugrainSüdsüdost, om morgen stille och wklardt siden lidett fog regnn, item mere regn om efftermeddag.p. 158
1 SepNWauroraNordvest smuckt stille och klardt, mod afften nordost, om natten klardt och store casmata y norden. Abiit Rothmannus.p. 158
2 SepSEaurora, overcastSudwest, nogit graade och lidett Solskien om dagen undertiden mod afften Sudost, forst om natten nogit klardt blessinde och Casmata.p. 158
3 SepSEovercastSudost, themelige graade och solskien, mod afften wklardt och om natten. Accessit Hafnia studiosus qvidam Olay. Mgi. Sacericlis famulus.p. 158
4 SepNErain, overcastOsten, om morgen regn och nogit lidett graade, siden sudost morckt, Item regn om Meddagstiide, mod afftenn stille; den gannske dag vklardt, om natten nordost, nogit graade. Discessit famulus Saceridis.p. 158
5 SepNovercastVestenn themelige Stille och klardt, om natten nogitt stiernlyst, dog skyer och vklardt mesten y nordt.p. 158

Coloris sane inusitati & fere omnigeni, primum enim conspiciebantur ut soient flamea subalbescentia, postea rubra vel sanguinea, denique violi colorem induebant, coelique verti- cem culminabant dehinc partim ad septentrionem descendentia hemisphærium undique nostrum occupabant. 9The apparatus of the 1876 edition

The 1876 edition’s own apparatus, in the editors’ words: the footnotes under the diary text, by which F. R. Friis and H. F. Rørdam identified the abbreviated names, dated a death from another source, or marked where one scribe’s hand gives way to another; the five corrigenda printed after the text; and, drawn out of the footnotes, the changes of hand — the nearest thing to a scribal history of the codex until the manuscript itself is examined.

The footnotes 53

In the editors’ Danish, by printed page, with the notes of this register they were attached to (by page and name); a footnote no entry claims is listed with the entries on its page. Footnotes the scan’s text layer garbled beyond reading are omitted rather than reconstructed.

Tycho’s own movements

Rørdam’s entry for Tycho himself carries 106 page references, nearly all of them his departures for Copenhagen, Roskilde or Scania and his returns. The register excludes them by rule (§1). Extracted, they would give the diary’s own itinerary of the Hven years, to be reconciled with the stays in the Loca pillar.

Notes met in verification and not yet entered

  • 18 August 1586, p. 75: P. Ulrici aduentus deneg. — the Duke of Mecklenburg’s arrival then denied, five days before he came.
  • 8 January 1597, p. 260: Abiit Nicolaus sartor in Cimbriam et cum Georgio Herlufsholmium — the tailor Nicolaus to Jutland, and to Herlufsholm with Jørgen.

Persons not securely identified 48 notes

46 notes are graded B and 2 C; 10 carry no expanded name at all (an initial, a description, a group). The C-grade notes: 14 Aug 1592 “Accesserunt Nie. 2 (?) Mag. Vlfeld N K. et (?) stud.”; 2 Aug 1593 “Holandus I. (?) D. I V. hue appulit.”. Identification will come from the Familia prosopography, the letters and the university matricula, not from the diary.

Readings to settle in the manuscript

Rørdam’s introduction to his register already corrects the print against sense — Eg. Gor. for Ego Cor(oniam) (pp. 89, 107), D. Isach pater Cor. for pastor Cor(onensis) (p. 175), Olay for Olaus (p. 158), lateris for lateribus (p. 181), abii for abiit (p. 143), Limert for Linert (p. 166) — and his footnotes leave Podbusk or Bilde (p. 169) and the initials I. D. I. V. (p. 213) open. The codex is digitised (ÖNB viewer, IIIF manifest); none of these has been checked against it for this chapter.

Authority and prosopography links

9 persons carry a VIAF id and 21 link to the Familia pillar, of 136 named persons in §4. The remainder are unlinked, not because no record exists but because none has been attached.

The concordances

The Opera Omnia concordance is at month precision, and 15 months (Dec 1584, Jan 1585, Jan 1587, Feb 1587, Feb 1588, Mar 1588, Aug 1589, Sep 1589, Jul 1592, Oct 1592, Nov 1592, Jan 1593, Feb 1593, Mar 1593, Mar 1594) are interpolated; a day-level concordance needs the two-column text of the 1927 volume read column by column. The Internet Archive scan is linked at item level only, its text layer being too poor to map its leaves to the print.

The weather record

The flags are keyword-derived and unreviewed. Four entries still carry a following day’s text inside their own (a weekday glyph the parser does not know); the entries of 1 June 1588 and a handful of others whose day line the scan broke are absent from the day register and stand only in the notes that cite them. The 1876 text is letter-for-letter by the editor’s intent; the scan’s text layer behind this chapter is not, and the Danish here has not been proof-read against the scan.

11Sources

Each source with what it contributes to this chapter. Links are given only where they were opened and found to resolve.

  1. ÖNB, Cod. 10718
    Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Vienna, Cod. 10718 (Han), the manuscript of the meteorological diary kept at Uraniborg, 1 October 1582 – 22 April 1597; a 'Sammelhandschrift' of 191 leaves in quarto, bound in a fragment of a thirteenth-century parchment manuscript over pasteboard; bought for the Emperor Rudolf II, probably on 28 October 1601 (Jahrbuch der kunsthistorischen Sammlungen 1894, nos. 11755–11756), and in the Hofbibliothek by 1652 at the latest (Cod. 13555, fol. 154v).
    Contributes The object itself. Every entry in this chapter is a reading of this manuscript at one remove, through the 1876 print; the digitised codex is where a doubtful reading (Rørdam's 'Podbusk' or 'Bilde', the initials 'I. D. I. V.') must finally be settled.
    Open copy ÖNB digital viewer · IIIF Presentation manifest (v3) · catalogue record AC13957482
  2. Friis (ed.) 1876
    Tyge Brahes meteorologiske Dagbog, holdt paa Uraniborg for Aarene 1582–1597. Udgiven som Appendix til Collectanea Meteorologica af det Kgl. Danske Videnskabernes Selskab ved dets meteorologiske Comité. Copenhagen: H. H. Thiele, 1876. IV + 263 + LXXV pp. The diary text (pp. 1–263) was edited from the Vienna manuscript by F. R. Friis, with footnotes partly supplied by H. F. Rørdam; corrigenda ('Rettelser og Tillæg') on p. 264.
    Contributes The text every entry is taken from: the historical notes verbatim, the page on which each stands, and the editors' footnotes identifying persons. This chapter's page numbers are the printed pages of this volume.
    Cited by 248 entries
    Open copy Royal Danish Academy — the volume's page, with the PDF scan (Særpublikationer) · Internet Archive scan (University of Toronto copy) · contemporary notice, Historisk Tidsskrift
  3. Rørdam 1876 (Register)
    H. F. Rørdam, 'Register til de historiske Notitser, indførte i Tyge Brahes meteorologiske Dagbog for Aarene 1582–1597', in Friis (ed.) 1876, pp. XLVIII–LIV.
    Contributes The edition's own index of the historical notes: every person and place Rørdam could identify, with the printed pages on which each occurs. It is the prior catalogue this register is concorded against (§6), and the measure of what remains unextracted (§10).
  4. la Cour 1876
    Poul la Cour, 'Sammendrag af Veir-Iagttagelserne i Tyge Brahes meteorologiske Dagbog', in Friis (ed.) 1876, pp. I–XLVII, with the French 'Résumé d'un journal météorologique … tenu à Uraniborg', pp. LV–LXXV.
    Contributes The meteorological analysis of the diary: monthly tables, the classification of the Danish weather vocabulary (the graded wind terms, p. LXVII), and the comparison with the Copenhagen series of 1842–74. The weather section's glossary follows him.
  5. Opera Omnia IX (1927)
    Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia, ed. J. L. E. Dreyer, tom. IX (Copenhagen: Gyldendal, 1927; ed. Hans Raeder after Dreyer's death), pp. 1–146: 'Mutationes aëris a mense Octobri anni 1582 ad mensem Aprilem anni 1597', re-edited from Cod. 10718; with the editors' notes (pp. 317 ff.), an 'Index vocum Danicarum' (pp. 329–343) and an 'Index hominum inter Mutationes aëris commemoratorum' (pp. 344–348).
    Contributes The second edition of the diary and the one most libraries hold. §6 concords every month of this register to its page in this volume; the Index hominum is the second prior index of the persons.
  6. Christianson 2000
    John Robert Christianson, On Tycho's Island: Tycho Brahe and His Assistants, 1570–1601 (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2000).
    Contributes The modern prosopography of the household and its visitors, built on this diary among other sources (the 'steady flow of visitors, messengers, and prospective students', p. 74); the Familia pillar, to which the register's familia links lead, follows it.
  7. Thoren 1990
    Victor E. Thoren, with contributions by John R. Christianson, The Lord of Uraniborg: A Biography of Tycho Brahe (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1990).
    Contributes The narrative context of the great visits — James VI on 20 March 1590 and the Duke of Brunswick two months later (pp. 335–336) — and the reminder that the diary is not a complete visitor log: members of James's entourage made trips to Hven 'that were not recorded in Tycho's diary' (p. 335).
